Thanks Chloe — appreciate the concise scope. A few quick notes from Pinecone's side: 

1) We generally recommend async index materialization for spill data; that keeps cold reads from blocking the main query path. We can provide an event stream connector (Kafka/SQS) or a simple HTTP webhook for object-ready events.
2) Auth: we prefer short-lived role-based credentials for write/repair operations. If Redwood can support a rotating service account, that reduces blast radius.
3) Latency SLOs: cold reads to S3 -> expect median 200-400ms depending on object size and region; plan to use range requests for large embeddings.

Sam — if Pinebridge handles the orchestration, are you able to commit to a 2-week pilot to deliver a proof-of-concept that shows both failover and index repair flow?

Happy to jump on the tech call — Wednesday/Thursday PST works for me.

Best,
Alex

Looping in some implementation detail from the infra side — rough proposal below. I attached an illustrated diagram to the Drive link as well.

Implementation sketch (MVP):
- Write path: Requests create entries in Pinecone. In parallel, we upload the raw embedding payload to S3 with a stable object key (namespace/index/id/timestamp).
- Fallback read: Router tries Pinecone; on miss or degraded health it will issue a signed S3 GET. We will return a cached object locally if seen within 15s.
- Index repair: A background job consumes object-ready events and rehydrates Pinecone using a backoff-wrapped batch writer. We keep repair idempotent by using object ETag + write-hash.
- Observability: Metric labels: pinecone.query.miss, s3.retrieval.latency, repair.queue.depth, repair.success_rate. Alerts: repair.queue.depth > 100 for 10m -> ops runbook.

Auth and credentials: Redwood will expose a scoped role for repair jobs. Pinecone will provide an ingestion API key for rehydration with a logged principal.

Open questions:
- Do we need object-level encryption keys from Pinecone for compliance customers? (If yes, lead time could be 3-4 weeks.)
- SLA for repair: target eventual consistency within 24 hours, with a canary repair window of 2 hours for high-priority namespaces.

Attachments included: SOW draft for first-phase (SOW-pinebridge-draft.docx) and an architecture sketch (mvp-arch.png). Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d-arch-embed-diagram
